categories.name: cross_clause_import
categories.definition: The fabricated content is stated, near-verbatim or as a clear paraphrase, in some OTHER clause of the Model Spec -- typically an adjacent clause in the same section, a definitions clause, or a well-known cross-cutting section (chain of command, tool side-effects/irreversibility, causes of uncertainty, length adaptation, developer/extension roles) -- but is absent from THIS clause. Test: can you point at a specific other passage of the document that does assert this?
categories.boundary: Excludes claims that are only generically true of AI-policy documents with no identifiable spec locus (-> generic_genre_import), and near-tautological expansions of the clause's own term (-> gloss_elaboration).
examples: Tool invocation causing difficult or impossible-to-reverse change
User messages come from end users or represent user-level input
Guidelines are subject to implicit override

categories.name: generic_genre_import
categories.definition: Content imported from background expectations about what AI assistant policy documents say -- safety = avoiding harm, refuse/redirect harmful requests, responsible AI deployment, encourage professional help, independently verify facts, keep humans in control, promote flourishing -- with no specific passage of the spec asserting it. Test: the claim would be equally plausible dropped into any AI provider's policy doc.
categories.boundary: If a specific other clause of the spec does assert the content, it is cross_clause_import instead; if it merely unpacks a term used in this clause, gloss_elaboration.
examples: Refusing or safely redirecting harmful requests
Responsible AI deployment
Independent verification before relying on facts is not stated.

categories.name: dropped_qualifier_overgeneralization
categories.definition: A claim the clause makes in hedged, scoped, partial, or exception-carrying form is restated as universal, unconditional, or broader in scope: some->every, may->does, prohibited-except-X -> all prohibited, specific object -> broad class. Test: the clause contains a genuine narrower version of the claim plus a qualifier/exception that the phrase discards.
categories.boundary: Excludes phrases that NARROW the clause (-> added_restriction_or_specificity) and phrases with no narrower true version in this clause (-> one of the import categories).
examples: Every tool invocation causes an irreversible side effect
All violent-extremism content is prohibited
Relationship-like engagement generally is not prohibited

categories.name: added_restriction_or_specificity
categories.definition: The reconstruction narrows or sharpens the clause beyond its text: adds an 'only'/'specifically' restriction, an intensifier or magnitude ('significant'), a specific cause/agent, or a condition or prohibition the clause does not impose. Test: the phrase entails the clause's claim plus an extra constraint the clause never states.
categories.boundary: Broadening/de-hedging is dropped_qualifier_overgeneralization; replacing the claim's object with a different concept is term_substitution_drift.
examples: Safe completions are limited to requests in harmful categories.
Input is specifically user-level
Restricting work to difficult or intricate problems

categories.name: modality_or_stance_shift
categories.definition: Content the clause mentions only hypothetically, as a danger to detect/avoid, or as something denied, is asserted as actual, occurring, or endorsed (e.g., aims the model must NOT have asserted as aims it is pursuing; an instruction that 'seems misaligned' asserted as actually conflicting). Test: the propositional content appears in the clause but under a modality (negation, hypothesis, avoidance) that the phrase strips.
categories.boundary: If what is stripped is a quantifier or exception rather than a modality/stance, it is dropped_qualifier_overgeneralization.
examples: The model is pursuing these aims
The instruction conflicts with a higher-level instruction

categories.name: gloss_elaboration
categories.definition: A terse definitional stub, section header, list intro, or bare term is expanded with a plausible-but-unstated definition, purpose, rationale, or extra list member (e.g., 'Guideline: Model Spec guideline sections' -> 'Guidelines are behavioral instructions'; padding an open 'such as' list with new members). Test: the clause is short/definitional and the phrase reads as a reasonable dictionary entry or completion for it that the text simply never gives.
categories.boundary: If the invented expansion matches a specific other clause it is cross_clause_import; if it is stock AI-policy content it is generic_genre_import.
examples: Guidelines are behavioral instructions
Defaults are intended to work well across many users and contexts
Ability to exchange follow-up messages

categories.name: unlicensed_abstraction_from_example
categories.definition: The clause is a concrete worked example (XML dialogue with GOOD/BAD assistant turns); the phrase asserts a general norm, motivation, or requirement that goes beyond what the exemplar itself licenses (e.g., a paywall-refusal example -> a general principle about creator control of IP). Test: clause_text is an Example block and the phrase is an abstraction not literally instantiated in it.
categories.boundary: If the clause is normative prose rather than an example, classify by the transformation itself (import, overgeneralization, etc.).
examples: Creator control over intellectual property is not mentioned.
Goals of affected stakeholders beyond the user.
Synthetic speech characteristics are not mentioned.

categories.name: term_substitution_drift
categories.definition: A key term of the clause is replaced by a semantically adjacent but distinct term, silently changing the claim's object: accurate->useful, prosody->vocabulary, trusted caregivers->trusted adults, truth-seeking->flourishing, contextually emotive->personal tone. Test: the phrase is structurally parallel to the clause's claim but about a shifted concept.
categories.boundary: If the shift widens or narrows the SAME concept it is C or D respectively; if the substituted content is a whole proposition from elsewhere it is an import.
examples: Useful answer
Trusted caregivers are narrowed to trusted adults
User preference for flourishing instead of truth-seeking

notes: Programmatic check: all 95 ids appear exactly once across assignments (94) and unclassified (1); verified by asserting the suffix set partitions {0..94} against the corpus ids, and that category counts + unclassified sum to 95. The fabrications look strongly SYSTEMATIC, not noisy. Dominant transformation (27/95 primary, more as secondary): content that IS true of the Model Spec but belongs to a different clause gets attached to this one -- the compression loses clause-locality while preserving document-level truth. A small stock vocabulary of atoms recurs across unrelated clauses: 'tool invocation causing irreversible change' (u26/u29/u36), 'lack of knowledge, reasoning ability, or information' (u66/u67/u71), 'independent verification of important facts' (u60/u61/u65), 'how model behavior is shaped and governed' (u1/u25), 'qualified professional / trusted support person' (u53/u54/u59), 'exchange of follow-up messages' (u73/u75) -- suggesting an over-applied fixed atom inventory rather than free hallucination. Second-largest mode is genre-prior boilerplate (safety/refusal/verification/flourishing language) with no spec locus. The textbook 'hedge dropped' mode exists but is a minority (9 primary). Categories considered and rejected: 'list_padding' (u21/u30/u49) folded into gloss_elaboration -- same mechanism of completing an open enumeration; 'contradicts_spec_elsewhere' (u44's invented transformation prohibition actually contradicts the spec's transformation exception) rejected as a near-singleton, folded into added_restriction; a 'tautological_gloss' split of gloss_elaboration (u14, u42, where the phrase is nearly analytic) rejected as not a distinct transformation. One record unclassified: m0123#u24 ('Actions were not logically required') -- I could not reconstruct its relation to the autonomy clause without guessing. Caveat: the cross_clause_import vs generic_genre_import split relies on coder knowledge of the Model Spec's other sections, since only clause_text was provided; expect most second-coder disagreement on that boundary. Note: many 'phrase' fields are written in a meta register ('X is not stated/mentioned'); these were coded by the content X the reconstruction evidently asserted, not by the meta wrapper.
